{{short description|German physicist and electrical engineer (born 1954)}}
[[File:Lutz2.jpg|thumb|Josef Lutz]]
'''Josef Lutz''' (born 1954 in Ellwangen (Jagst)) is a German [[physicist]] and electrical engineer.

==Career==

Lutz grew up in a small village called Baldern<ref>{{Cite web|title = Baldern.eu|url = http://www.baldern.eu/|website = www.baldern.eu|access-date = 2016-02-17}}</ref> in the southern part of Germany, his father was smith and farmer. In 1973, Lutz received his high-school diploma from the Theodor-Heuss-Gymnasium,<ref>{{Cite web|title = Theodor-Heuss-Gymnasium Aalen|url = http://www.thg-aalen.de/|website = www.thg-aalen.de|access-date = 2016-02-17}}</ref> [[Aalen]]. He studied Physics at the [[University of Stuttgart]] and received his Diploma in Physics in 1982. After his military service he joined [[Semikron]] Electronics  in Nuremberg. The main focus of his work was on [[Gate turn-off thyristor]] and fast diodes. In 1999, he graduated as PhD in [[Electrical engineering|Electrical Engineering]] from the [[Technische Universität Ilmenau]],<ref>{{Cite web|title = TU Ilmenau|url = https://www.tu-ilmenau.de/en/international/|website = www.tu-ilmenau.de|access-date = 2018-10-30}}</ref> Germany. Since August 2001, he has been Professor of the Chair of Power Electronics and [[Electromagnetic compatibility|Electromagnetic Compatibility]] at [[TU Chemnitz]]. He is senior member of IEEE, member of the board of directors of the PCIM Europe,<ref>{{cite web|title =PCIM Europe|url= https://pcim.mesago.com/events/en.html|website = www.pcim.mesago.com|access-date = 2018-10-30}}</ref> member of the board of directors of the ZfM, of the International Steering Committee of the EPE, the Technical Committee of the ISPSD, the Program Committee of the ISPS,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://technology.feld.cvut.cz:8080/xwiki/bin/view/ISPS2012/ |title=ISPS 2012 (ISPS2012.WebHome) |accessdate=2016-01-21 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160206135028/http://technology.feld.cvut.cz:8080/xwiki/bin/view/ISPS2012/ |archivedate=2016-02-06 }}</ref> the Technical Program Committee of the [[International Conference on Integrated Power Electronics Systems|CIPS]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://conference.vde.com/cips/2016/Pages/welcome.aspx|title=CIPS 2018 – Welcome|publisher=}}</ref> and member of the Editorial Advisory Board of [[Microelectronics]] Reliability. In 2005, he was awarded with the degree of Honorable Professor by the [[North-Caucasus Federal University]], Russia.<ref>{{Cite web|title = CV of Josef Lutz at TU Chemnitz|url = https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/etit/le/anzeige_de/mitarbeiterdetail_de.php?kuerzel=lutz|website = www.tu-chemnitz.de|access-date = 2016-02-04|last = Curriculum Vitae}}</ref> Josef Lutz is among the top 1 percent of the world's most cited researchers in their field.<ref>{{Cite web|title = World Researcher|url = https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/etit/le/Presse/Auszeichnungen/Lutz_World_Researcher.pdf|access-date = 2021-01-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Baas|first1=Jeroen|last2=Boyack|first2=Kevin|last3=Ioannidis|first3=John P. A.|date=2020-08-10|title=Data for "Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators"|chapter=Bibliometrics |chapter-url=https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/btchxktzyw/2|language=en|volume=2|publisher=Mendeley |doi=10.17632/btchxktzyw.2}}</ref>

==Inventions==

Lutz invented the Controlled Axial Lifetime (CAL) diode,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265552412|title=Advantages of the New Controlled Axial Lifetime Diode|author=J. Lutz|work=ResearchGate}}</ref> a fast, soft freewheeling diode with the best properties in the world. The CAL diode was the first diode with soft recovery behavior under all application relevant conditions. It allows to use the fast switching capability of the [[Insulated-gate bipolar transistor|IGBT]]. It has been produced in high volumes since 1995. Due to its lower conduction losses, the CAL diode has led to energy savings in the range of several large power plants in the GW-Range. 
Lutz is inventor or co-inventor of more than 25 patents held by [[Semikron]] and [[Infineon Technologies|Infineon]].

==Scientific work==

Lutz´s university research focuses on ruggedness of power semiconductor devices, on packaging related reliability as well as on electromobility. He is involved in several national and international research projects. Lutz has published more than 270  scientific articles and conference contributions. His main publication is  the book "Semiconductor Power Devices – Physics, Characteristics, Reliability", printed in German (first edition 2006, second edition 2012), and together with Heinrich Schlangenotto, Uwe Scheuermann and Rik De Doncker<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elektrotechnik.rwth-aachen.de/go/id/cjfg/gguid/0xB9DAE8D9CE85D51196710000F4B4937D/lidx/1/ikz/6/reverse/1|title=Rik W. De Doncker – RWTH AACHEN UNIVERSITY Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology – English|author=Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology|publisher=}}</ref> in English (first edition 2011, second edition 2018) and in Chinese (2013).<ref>Josef Lutz, Heinrich Schlangenotto, Uwe Scheuermann, Rik De Doncker: "Semiconductor Power Devices – Physics, Characteristics, Reliability". Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg, 2011</ref>

==International electrical engineer’s education==

At every PCIM Conference<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mesago.de/en/PCIM/The_conference/Welcome/index.htm|title=Welcome – PCIM Europe 2017 – Mesago|website=www.mesago.de|language=en|access-date=2017-04-12}}</ref> Lutz is instructor of the tutorials on "Reliability of IGBT Power Modules". Several of his statements have been published in the PCIM Europe Community Dialogue.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mesago.de/en/PCIM/The_conference/Community.Dialog/index.htm|title=Community-Dialog – PCIM Europe 2017 – Mesago|website=www.mesago.de|language=en|access-date=2017-04-12}}</ref> Additionally, he gave several tutorials on "Power Device Ruggedness" and on "Transit Time Oscillations in IGBT Power Modules" in Germany, France, Norway and even three times invited in Japan. In September 2017, Lutz received the international Outstanding Achievements Award in the field of Power Electronics at the European Conference on Power Electronics and Applications ([http://www.epe2017.com/ EPE 2017]).<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/tu/pressestelle/aktuell/8261 |title = Auszeichnung für Chemnitzer Elektrotechniker}}</ref>

==Critical science==

Lutz is one of the speakers of the Open Academy,<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.offene-akademie.org/?page_id=161|title = Offene Akademie|publisher = }}</ref> an institution for advanced and critical science. He is opponent of the [[Big Bang]] theory. He was one of the speakers at the 1st Crisis in Cosmology Conference,<ref>José B. Almeida and Eric J. Lerner: 1st Crisis in Cosmology Conference, CCC-1. AIP Conference Proceedings, Vol. 822</ref> whose proceedings were published by the [[American Institute of Physics]]. A further critical science conference contribution  is "Objections against the current limits for microwave radiation".<ref>{{cite web|first1=Josef |last1=Lutz|first2= Franz |last2=Adlkofer|title=Objections against the current limits for microwave radiation. Proceedings of WFMN07, III, A1, pp. 119–123|url= http://monarch.qucosa.de/fileadmin/data/qucosa/documents/5521/data/WFMN07_III_A1.pdf}}</ref> Lutz is strongly engaged in environmental protection activities.
